name: Bryan Steil
page_title: Bryan Steil's Issue Positions (Political Courage Test)
on_the_ballot: Running, Republican for U.S. House (WI) - District 1

positions.question: Do you support the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade?

evidence.text: "I am proudly pro-life. We must work to cherish and protect the sanctity of life at its most vulnerable stages. The recent Supreme Court ruling was a victory for life and returns these important decisions back to the people and their elected representatives in the states. At the federal level, I am standing up for life by supporting proposals like the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act and leading efforts to prevent taxpayer funding for abortion."
Rated 100% by National Right to Life Committee
Voted against HR 8296: "Women's Health Protection Act of 2022"
Voted in favor of HR 26: "Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act"

evidence.text: "We can promote reasonable and responsible spending cuts to save taxpayer dollars, protect Social Security and Medicare, and promote financial stability. It’s time for President Biden to come to the negotiating table."
"We made a promise to support our seniors. I am working to protect and preserve Social Security and Medicare. Thanks to @AARP for the productive conversation."
Rated 0% by National Committee to Preserve Social Security and Medicare

positions.question: Do you support protecting government officials, including law enforcement officers, from personal liability in civil lawsuits concerning alleged misconduct?

evidence.text: "Our law enforcement officers put their lives on the line each day to keep our communities safe. We must always support our nation’s police."
Voted against HR 1280 "George Floyd Justice in Policing Act of 2021."

"It is my priority to ensure that our communities in Southeast Wisconsin are safe places to live and raise a family. Throughout my time in Congress, I have continually met with local government leaders, members of law enforcement, and people across Southeast Wisconsin to examine how we can keep our communities safe. I have strongly opposed the "Defund the Police" movement, which is a dangerous scheme that had made communities across our country less safe. We must support the men and women who have taken the oath to protect and serve our communities."

positions.question: Do you support federal spending as a means of promoting economic growth (e.g. grants, tax incentives)?

evidence.text: "Families and workers are being clobbered by rising costs at the grocery store and at the gas pump. I’m fighting against wasteful spending and working to lower gas prices by unleashing American energy independence."

"Washington spends too much of our money. The out of control spending is contributing to higher prices and rising inflation. We must end the massive government spending coming from Congress. I believe we need a long term, process driven solution to fix the spending problem. We need to restore fiscal discipline to the budget process while also continuing pro-growth policies to unleash the full strength of the American economy."
Voted against HR 5376: "Inflation Reduction Act of 2022"
Voted in favor of HR 2811: "Limit, Save, Grow Act"

positions.question: Do you support the federal government increasing funding for affordable housing programs?

evidence.text: "I’m working to make housing more affordable as prices continue to rise."

"The rising cost of housing is putting an added strain on workers and families. I joined affordable housing leaders in Janesville for a discussion on how we can work to lower costs and increase supply."
Voted against HR 7301: "Emergency Housing Protections and Relief Act of 2020"

positions.question: Do you support the federal government taking action, beyond those of the Federal Reserve, to alleviate inflation?

evidence.text: "Bidenomics isn't working. Wisconsin families are spending $709 more every month than they did two years ago. President Biden’s visit today is just a reminder that everyone is paying more for their everyday needs after the Inflation Reduction Act passed."
"Biden’s policies have driven inflation higher. Our bill limits spending and saves taxpayer money."
"Deficit spending increased by $320 billion over last year. Inflation has increased 17% over three years, driving up costs for families. I’m working to get government spending under control"
Voted against HR 5376: "Inflation Reduction Act of 2022"

positions.question: Do you support the forgiveness of federal student loan debt?

evidence.text: "Biden’s plan to cancel student loans are just one example of the Admin’s efforts to unilaterally spend your tax dollars. We need to put a check on the Biden Administration and require them to disclose their executive actions impact on inflation."
"Forcing taxpayers to pay for student loan debt doesn’t fix the underlying problem—the rising costs of higher education, in particular, living expenses—it only encourages more spending!"
Rated 0% by National Education Association

positions.question: Do you support requiring a government-issued identification in order to vote at the polls?

positions.question: Do you support increasing security along the southern US border?

evidence.text: "We need to secure our border. In the past two years, drug and human trafficking has skyrocketed at our southern border. Bad actors from all over the world are taking advantage of our lax security – including drug dealers, human traffickers, and individuals with terrorist affiliations. Deadly illicit fentanyl is coming across in record numbers, wreaking havoc in communities and families right here in Wisconsin. I have visited the US-Mexico border, spoken directly with border protection officers and have seen the crisis first hand. Securing our border is a matter of national security. We need to build a wall, fund our border patrol officers, and finally secure our southern border."
Rated 83% by NumbersUSA
Voted in favor of HR 2: "Secure the Border Act of 2023"
Voted in favor of HR 5525: "Continuing Appropriations and Border Security Enhancement Act, 2024"
